item.title: New Pentagon Inspector General Report Highlights F-35 Shortfalls
item.description: The inspector general’s report criticized Lockheed Martin’s systemic inability to meet contract requirements, as well as the F-35’s dismal readiness rate. The post New Pentagon Inspector General Report Highlights F-35 Shortfalls appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: France, UK Pledge Troops to Defend Ukraine—but Only After War Ends
item.description: Even the most optimistic estimates suggest that Britain and France could only scrape together 15,000 troops for deployment in Ukraine—far too few to deter a future Russian invasion. The post France, UK Pledge Troops to Defend Ukraine—but Only After War Ends appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The US Navy Is Beefing Up Its SEAL Annual Physical Fitness Test
item.description: The new test is unlikely to be much of an issue, as Navy SEALs are among the most physically fit people on the planet. The post The US Navy Is Beefing Up Its SEAL Annual Physical Fitness Test appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The US Navy Is Quietly Building Up a Drone Fleet
item.description: The US Navy operates a handful of fixed-wing and rotary drones, but has kept them in support roles, avoiding a wholesale replacement of its manned forces. The post The US Navy Is Quietly Building Up a Drone Fleet appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: How China’s Naval Exercises Are Designed to Strangle Taiwan
item.description: A recent series of military exercises around Taiwan hints at how China plans to cut off the island in the event of conflict—and prevent Japan from sending a relief force. The post How China’s Naval Exercises Are Designed to Strangle Taiwan appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: France’s Omnirole Rafale Fighter Could Soon Fly over Iraq
item.description: Iraq has long been fascinated by the Dassault Rafale fighter jet—with interest in operating the warplane dating back to the rule of longtime dictator Saddam Hussein. The post France’s Omnirole Rafale Fighter Could Soon Fly over Iraq appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: “Adaptive Cycle Engines” Could Be the Next Great Fighter Jet Advancement
item.description: Adaptive cycle engines are specially designed to alternate between efficiency and raw power—extending an aircraft’s range without compromising on speed during engagements. The post “Adaptive Cycle Engines” Could Be the Next Great Fighter Jet Advancement appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Does “Terrain-Following Radar” Still Matter?
item.description: The development of terrain-following radar was vital to allowing aircraft to safely fly at low altitudes, where they could remain undetected by enemy radar. The post Does “Terrain-Following Radar” Still Matter? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Did Russia Try to Move Two Submarine Nuclear Reactors into North Korea?
item.description: Last year, a Russian “shadow fleet” vessel transported two submarine nuclear reactors to an uncertain destination in the Far East—but it never arrived. The post Did Russia Try to Move Two Submarine Nuclear Reactors into North Korea? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The Middle East’s Top Challenges in 2026
item.description: The collapse of Iran’s regional influence in 2025 has opened up a new spectrum of potential conflicts in Syria, Yemen, and Lebanon that will define 2026. The post The Middle East’s Top Challenges in 2026 appeared first on The National Interest.
